item.title: Stop treating workers like animals - PS Employment tells Ram Sami
item.description: Ram Sami & Sons (Fiji) Ltd should stop treating workers like animals and start treating them like human beings, irrespective of whether they are from Bangladesh or Fiji. The rules should be the same for everyone. This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Employment Maritino Nemani as about 40 workers enter the second day of their strike.
item.content:encoded:
Ram Sami & Sons (Fiji) Ltd should stop treating workers like animals and start treating them like human beings, irrespective of whether they are from Bangladesh or Fiji. The rules should be the same for everyone.

This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Employment Maritino Nemani as about 40 workers enter the second day of their strike.

They are demanding better working conditions, improved pay and recognition of the National Union of Workers as their representative.

While speaking to fijivillage News, Nemani says the company was fined about $15,000 in 2024 for carrying their staff in the same truck as they carry the chicken in.

He says following concerns raised by the workers, their OHS inspectors will be visiting the site today.

The Permanent Secretary also confirms that their chief meditator is conducting informal mitigation with the company and the union today.

Nemani hopes that the issue will be resolved today as workers need to be treated with respect.

Ram Sami & Sons (Fiji) Ltd is expected to provide a response later today.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm tonight
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm tonight. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm tonight.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm tomorrow on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Vosarogo accuses Narube of spreading false narrative on Rabuka’s CRC comments
item.description: Lands and Mineral Resources Minister Filimoni Vosarogo has accused Unity Fiji Leader Savenaca Narube of spreading a false and irresponsible narrative by claiming Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka used the CRC report to create fear and uncertainty over race and religion for political gain. Vosarogo says contrary to Narube’s claims, Rabuka did not spread hate, fear or threaten any community when he add
item.content:encoded:
Lands and Mineral Resources Minister Filimoni Vosarogo has accused Unity Fiji Leader Savenaca Narube of spreading a false and irresponsible narrative by claiming Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka used the CRC report to create fear and uncertainty over race and religion for political gain.

Vosarogo says contrary to Narube’s claims, Rabuka did not spread hate, fear or threaten any community when he addressed the nation on the Constitutional Review Commission report.

He says the Prime Minister did precisely the opposite, with his first message being an appeal for all Fijians to remain calm in response to racial and religious rhetoric already being pushed online.

Vosarogo says Narube has now chosen to claim that Rabuka deliberately used the CRC report to spread fear and uncertainty on race and religion for political gain.

He says nothing could be further from the truth and describes it as shocking that such a serious allegation was published on Unity Fiji’s official pages without evidence to support it.

Vosarogo says Narube’s comments are highly irresponsible, particularly given the sensitivity of race and religion in Fiji and the responsibility that comes with political leadership.

He says the irony is that Rabuka had specifically appealed to political leaders to be responsible with their words and not turn the national discussion surrounding the CRC report into a political, racial or religious battle.

Vosarogo says Narube has responded by doing exactly what political leaders were being asked not to do.

He also responds to Narube’s statement that there is no need to fracture Fiji again, saying Narube is right about that but needs to follow his own advice.

Vosarogo claims that through what he describes as false and irresponsible comments, Narube himself appears to be attempting to fracture the nation.

He is urging people to read Rabuka’s original message for themselves and make their own judgement on what the Prime Minister said.

Vosarogo says there is already enough misinformation and inflammatory rhetoric circulating in Fiji without political leaders adding to it.

He says political leaders can disagree, criticise each other, debate issues and offer different visions for Fiji, but there must be a line when it comes to dragging race and religion into political attacks based on claims that are not true.

Vosarogo says Fiji deserves political discourse that is robust but responsible, and those seeking to lead the country have a duty to contribute to that standard rather than undermine it.

item.title: One in 50 Fijian children could have rheumatic heart disease
item.description: Rheumatic heart disease, or RHD, can develop following rheumatic fever and can cause long-term damage to the heart valves. Children between five and 15 years old are considered most at risk in Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
Rheumatic heart disease, or RHD, can develop following rheumatic fever and can cause long-term damage to the heart valves.

Children between five and 15 years old are considered most at risk in Fiji.

The report says an average of 71 deaths a year have been attributed to RHD over the past 10 years, with the disease estimated to cost Fiji about $18 million annually in medical and other costs.

A major concern is that RHD can develop without obvious symptoms, meaning significant heart damage may have already occurred by the time a person becomes unwell.

Over the past five years, more than 13,000 school children, pregnant women and family members have been screened for RHD.

Screening has been introduced in schools and expanded into antenatal services to identify people at risk earlier and ensure they receive appropriate treatment and follow-up care.

Cure Kids Fiji Country Manager Dr Jimaima Kailawadoko-Matanaicake says every child deserves the opportunity to grow up healthy, learn, play and reach their full potential without RHD standing in their way.

She says the aim is to identify and care for more children early so fewer will require complex heart surgery later in life.

The programme is a partnership involving the Ministry of Health, Cure Kids and other regional partners, with support from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.
